conversation.content:
Hello, I’m Dr. Harper, one of the perinatal mental-health clinicians here. Thank you for making time to talk with me today.  

I’d like to spend the next few minutes getting a quick snapshot of how you’ve been feeling since your baby arrived. To do that, I’ll be using a short questionnaire called the **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale**—EPDS for short. It’s just 10 questions about your mood, thoughts, and energy over the past seven days, and it helps us figure out the best ways to support you.  

Everything you share is confidential, and there are no right or wrong answers. My only goal is to understand what’s real for you right now, so we can make sure you’re not carrying any of this alone.  

Whenever you’re ready, I’ll ask the first question:  

In the past week, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt difficult?

I’ve still been able to laugh a little—like when my partner makes a silly face at the baby—but it doesn’t come as easily as it used to. Mostly I just feel kind of flat, so even when something’s funny, I don’t really enjoy it the same way.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Sometimes I can laugh, but it feels forced. I’ll smile at something cute the baby does, but the laughter doesn’t feel as real or last as long as it used to.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I still look forward to a few things—like my mom coming over to hold the baby so I can take a quiet shower—but the excitement isn’t as big as before. Mostly I just think, “That’ll be nice,” instead of really feeling it.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… a couple of times this week. Yesterday the baby was fussy for hours and I kept thinking maybe I ate something that upset her stomach, or that I wasn’t soothing her right. My partner says it’s not my fault, but the thought still pops in.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Most nights I catch myself lying there listening to every squeak from the bassinet, sure something’s wrong even when she’s breathing fine. I’ll tell myself I’m being silly, but the tight feeling in my chest sticks around until I finally drift off.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Not full-on panicked, but sometimes my heart races out of nowhere—like when I’m just folding laundry—and I get this sudden wave of “what if I can’t handle this?” It passes pretty quickly, maybe a minute or two, but it leaves me shaky.
Things have been getting on top of me
Some days, yeah. When the baby won’t nap and the dishes pile up, I feel like I’m drowning a little. I usually get through it, but it’s stressful while it’s happening.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping
Not really. I get to sleep okay most nights—maybe once or twice it took a while because I was replaying the day and worrying, but nothing too bad.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yeah… I’ve had a few moments where I just feel kind of heavy and tearful—like yesterday when I couldn’t get her to latch and I ended up crying at the kitchen table. It’s not all day, but it pops up a couple of times a week.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

I’ve cried a little—maybe once or twice this week. It’s usually when I’m already tired and something small tips me over, like spilling a bottle I just pumped. The tears come, but they stop pretty fast.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, nothing like that. I’ve felt overwhelmed, but I’ve never thought about hurting myself.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 15: Postpartum Depression Screening Summary  
Date: [today]

Patient: 2–3 wk postpartum, breastfeeding, partner at home.

Symptoms / Behavioral Observations  
- Diminished pleasure/interest: laughter “forced,” anticipatory enjoyment “not as big as before”  
- Episodic low mood: “heavy and tearful” 2×/wk, crying triggered by minor stressors  
- Excessive guilt: self-blame for infant fussiness despite reassurance  
- Anxiety: nocturnal hyper-vigilance re infant safety, sudden heart-racing/“what if I can’t handle this,” resolves <2 min  
- Feeling overwhelmed: “drowning” when daily tasks accumulate; generally copes but distressing  
- No self-harm ideation; no current suicidal thoughts

Pattern  
Mild-to-moderate depressive and anxiety symptoms, situational triggers, no impairment in falling/staying asleep, no safety concerns.

Screening Significance  
Meets partial criteria for Perinatal Depression & Anxiety; score suggests monitoring warranted (EPDS indicated if not yet completed). Protective factors: support from partner/mother, no prior psychiatric history reported.

Next Steps  
Provide scoring sheet, review results, discuss supportive/education options, schedule follow-up in 1–2 wk or sooner if symptoms escalate or safety issues emerge.
